name: INTEGRAL
summary: ESA gamma-ray observatory whose high-resolution SPI spectrometer studies narrow decay-dark-matter lines and Galactic positron-annihilation radiation.
detection_principle: High-purity germanium spectroscopy and coded-aperture imaging compare line signals across sky regions and backgrounds to constrain photon-producing dark-matter decay.

sites.name: Highly elliptical Earth orbit; science mission ended
sites.location: Highly elliptical Earth orbit; science mission ended

status.label: Data taking ended / historical experiment
status.evidence: ESA's overview gives February 28 as the mission end date; the operational archive states that the final observing orbit spanned February 28 to March 1.

collaboration.name: INTEGRAL collaboration / mission team
collaboration.participants_note: Only examples of lead or participating institutions directly established by the sources are listed. This is not a complete collaboration list, and listing does not imply equal institutional roles.

results.summary: A large-sample narrow-line search constrains two-body dark-matter decay with at least one photon in the final state.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
